findings.title: Algorithm5.1 does not produce feasible probabilities

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.location: p. 15 Algorithm 5.1 lines 3–7; p. 2 Algorithm 1.2 initialization
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.type: Literal pseudocode: missing repeated thresholding and sparse-input branch
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.observation: The preservation block is a single if/end-if, although the preceding prose calls it recursive. There is no zero/already-sparse early return.
decisive_checks: For v=(100,90,1,1), m=3, the initial average is 192/3=64. If the single block preserves 100, the residual probability for 90 is 2*90/92=45/23>1. If instead it preserves 90, the probability for 100 is 2*100/102=100/51>1. Both eligible choices violate the line-7 requirement p in [0,1]^n.
The repeated procedure preserves both 100 and 90, then uses residual probabilities (1/2,1/2), giving the valid outputs (100,90,2,0) and (100,90,0,2), each with probability 1/2.

For a zero vector with at least two entries and an ordinary m>=1, the single block can select a zero coordinate because 0>=0; the remaining formula divides zero by a zero tail sum. Algorithm 1.2 actually calls this case at its first step because x_0=0.
counterevidence: The p. 14 prose describes a recursive construction, and the optimal q* characterization on p. 17 requires thresholding until the condition fails. These identify the intended correction.
The pinned rsri.py lines 33–36 returns an unchanged copy whenever nnz(v)<=m. Lines 42–48 repeatedly recompute the preservation threshold, so it does not have the printed one-pass omission.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.proposed_correction: Return v if nnz(v)<=m; otherwise replace the single if by a repeated preservation loop with a positive residual budget and sum, then sample only the remaining fractional probabilities.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.scope: The literal supplied pseudocode fails its output specification on admissible small inputs. This is not a counterexample to the intended pivotal sparsification used in the mathematical proof.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.grading: Materiality must be assessed at the algorithm specification and downstream dependency level; no severity is assigned merely from the ease of replacing if with while.

findings.severity_reason: The explicit central algorithm fails its advertised domain/output specification, including actual zero initialization. Intended recursive prose and code are counterevidence limiting the claim to printed specification.
findings.scope_limit: Specific acquired version and stated location only; not a general rejection of the intended RSRI convergence theory.

findings.title: Algorithm5.2 omits complementary carry assignment

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.location: p. 16 Algorithm 5.2 line 6 and deterministic-probability boundary
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.type: Literal pseudocode: omitted complementary carry assignment
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.observation: Line 6 assigns ell=h with a stated probability but gives no assignment for the complementary outcome. The subsequent condition tests the persistent value ell==h.

decisive_trace.input: p=(3/5,3/5,4/5), m=2, with the empty-prefix convention needed for the streaming algorithm.
decisive_trace.first_step: u=1, h=1, updated b=1/5. The stated assignment probability is (3/5-1/5)/(1-1/5)=1/2. On assignment, ell=1 and S={2}; without assignment, ell remains 0 and S={1}.
decisive_trace.second_step: The carry is the only leading candidate before p_3. Thus h equals the old ell. Regardless of whether line 6 performs its assignment, the test ell==h succeeds, so index 3 is selected.
decisive_trace.literal_distribution: {1,3} and {2,3}, each with probability 1/2; hence inclusion marginals (1/2,1/2,1), not (3/5,3/5,4/5). The failed first assignment also leaves positive carry mass on the sentinel index 0.
decisive_trace.corrected_distribution: With the complementary ell=u+1 assignment, the distribution is {1,2}:1/5, {1,3}:2/5, {2,3}:2/5, giving exactly the required marginals.
decisive_trace.boundary: At a deterministic leading p_i=1 with zero carry, the printed weighted draw can have total leading mass zero (or the maximum defining u is empty without an empty-prefix convention). Deterministic inclusions and zero probabilities should be processed explicitly. Algorithm 5.1 itself can supply p_i=1.

counterevidence: The two-outcome pivotal calculation in PIV-C3 shows the intended complementary assignment.

The retained code lines 76–80 explicitly selects the left and updates the survivor to the right in one branch, and selects the right while retaining the left in the other. Lines 83–91 handle the final residual selection.

In an exact-arithmetic reading, this retained control flow gives the corrected three-set distribution for the test probabilities. No author-code execution or claim of general floating-point correctness is made.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.proposed_correction: Specify both carry assignments, including ell=u+1 with complementary probability, and document deterministic-probability/empty-prefix cases.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.scope: The evidence concerns the literal pseudocode and its stated unbiased marginals. The intended standard pivotal method remains consistent with Theorem 5.1.

findings.severity_reason: Literal core sampling algorithm violates unbiased marginals required by downstream mean/variance analysis. The actual retained implementation contains the intended two branches.

findings.title: Pinned implementation can exhaust residual sampling budget

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.type: Static boundary failure of the relaxed preservation test in the retained implementation
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.precise_issue: The factor 1-1e-8 can mark m entries for exact preservation while positive residual mass remains. The next iteration then divides by m-|keep|=0.
static_trace: Use a floating-valued vector v=(1,1,10^(-9)) and m=2; nnz(v)=3 so the function enters its sparsification branch.

On the first preservation pass the mathematical threshold is (2+10^(-9))/2=1+5*10^(-10). Multiplying by 1-10^(-8) gives a value strictly below 1, by approximately 9.5*10^(-9). Thus both unit entries satisfy the line-44 relaxed comparison, while the small positive entry does not.
The keep count becomes 2. The second pass of range(m) reaches line 43 with positive residual numerator 10^(-9) and zero denominator 2-2.
This is an exact arithmetic/control-flow demonstration of the zero denominator. No author code was imported or run, and no observed runtime exception or warning is claimed.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.alternative_readings: The tolerance is evidently intended to stabilize an equality test, but it changes which entries may be declared exactly preserved. Ordinary exact pivotal thresholding would retain no unit entry at this initial threshold and has no zero denominator on this input.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.proposed_correction: Ensure the preservation decision cannot consume all residual slots while nonzero mass remains; retain strict feasibility of the residual probabilities and handle any numerical tie policy explicitly.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.scope: This is a defect in the actual pinned implementation's boundary handling. It does not refute the mathematical pivotal construction or its optimality theorem. Code evidence should not be described as globally correct merely because it repairs the two printed omissions.

findings.severity_reason: The actual supplied numerical routine reaches positive residual mass divided by zero on an admissible vector. This is static control-flow evidence, not an executed exception or main-theorem counterexample.

findings.title: Auxiliary normalization and local statement corrections

corollary.location: p. 20 Corollary 5.5, compared with the explicitly normalized proof on p. 19
corollary.type: Missing normalization in a stated scalar sparsification-error bound
corollary.precise_issue: The corollary quantifies arbitrary u,v with nonnegative coordinatewise real and imaginary products but omits ||u||_infinity<=1. Its display uses an undefined f; even interpreting f=u as the intended notation does not restore the missing normalization.
corollary.decisive_counterexample: Take v=(1,1), m=1 and u=(3,0). Correct pivotal sparsification returns (2,0) or (0,2), each with probability 1/2. Both sign conditions hold. Then E|u*(phi(v)-v)|^2=9, whereas the finite i=0 candidate on the stated right side is (1+1)^2=4, so its minimum cannot support the claimed bound. This argument uses the intended correct pivotal operator, not the defective printed implementation.
corollary.counterevidence: The proof of Theorem 5.1 explicitly starts with ||u||_infinity<=1 and explicitly uses it in the final variance bound. The main theorem's triple norm already incorporates this normalization.
corollary.proposed_correction: Use f=u consistently and require ||u||_infinity<=1, or multiply the right side by ||u||_infinity^2.
corollary.dependency_limit: The primary executor must assess where this corollary is used later in Section 6. This bounded helper has not independently determined that downstream dependency and does not claim a failure of Theorem 5.1 or the main solver convergence theorem.

g_difference_identity.observation: The printed equality for g(q)-g(q+1) omits a term.
g_difference_identity.exact_check: For m=2,q=0,v=(2,1,1), g(0)=16/2=8, g(1)=4, so the left side is 4. The printed product is (2/(2-0-1))*(2-4/2)=0.
g_difference_identity.correction: With k=m-q, S=sum tail magnitudes and a=next magnitude, the true difference is [-S^2+2kaS-ka^2]/[k(k-1)], or the printed product plus aS/k.
g_difference_identity.counterevidence: The monotonicity needed for the tail bound follows directly from a>=S/k, as shown in PIV-C6. Therefore this local algebra display does not refute Proposition 5.2.

distinct_indices.location: p. 18 equation (5.9) and p. 19 covariance wording
distinct_indices.observation: The written all-index range includes i=j, but negative correlation applies only to distinct indicators; for a nontrivial Bernoulli variable p<=p^2 is false. The variance proof subsequently retains diagonal variances separately and only needs the distinct-index property.
distinct_indices.classification: Local index-range clarification, not evidence against the intended negative-correlation proof.

undefined_tail_endpoint.observation: The denominator m-i requires an endpoint convention. For a positive remaining tail, one may regard the term as +infinity; for nnz(v)<=m, return v and use zero error directly. No distinct theorem counterexample is asserted from this notation.

findings.severity_reason: The corollary is literally false without normalization, but the immediately preceding proof states and uses the correct normalization and downstream formula retains its norm factor. Distinct-index and g-difference corrections have explicit valid adjacent arguments.
